title: With the setting off, Edit Customer shows the flag ticked and read-only
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure the Internal Work Orders setting is off in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A, flagged as an Internal customer, flagged while the setting was on.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer B, not flagged, so the two windows can be compared.
custom_steps:
1. Open customer A's page.
  2. Click Edit Customer on customer A's page.
  3. Click the "Settings" link in the line under the checkbox.
  4. Open customer B's page.
  5. Click Edit Customer on customer B's page.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The header shows no "Internal" badge.

Step 2:

  • "Internal customer" shows ticked and cannot be changed.
  • Under it the line reads "Turn on Internal Work Orders in Settings to change this."

Step 3:

  • Settings > Work Orders opens.

Step 4:

  • Customer B's page opens.

Step 5:

  • Customer B's Edit Customer window shows no "Internal customer" checkbox.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11758 (Story 1, Turn on Internal Work Orders, flag internal customers, manage categories)

  • S1-N4: “If the toggle is off, Edit Customer shows the checkbox only for a customer that already carries the flag, ticked and read-only, with the line "Turn on Internal Work Orders in Settings to change this." where Settings is a link; the Internal badge is hidden in the customer header, the customers list and the mobile card, so the read-only checkbox is the only trace of the flag. The flag has no effect on work orders until the toggle is on, and is removed by turning the setting on first.”
  • User Feedback Summary: “Setting off, flagged customer | "Turn on Internal Work Orders in Settings to change this." | Line under the read-only checkbox on Edit Customer”
